_about: Page-zone segmentation, *The Chukchee*'s tier: the text-column geometry the UI draws against and the tolerances measured on this book's 300-dpi scans, laid key by key over the workspace's ../config/zones.json, which holds the types, keys, actions and figure track every text shares. Read by harness/zones_config.py; consumed by both `harness zones` (validation) and the browser UI (drawing + client-side order warnings). Editing this file changes both, which is the point — none of it is hardcoded.

_provenance.measure: The text measure is a property of the book and is stable: over the 20 pages with line-precise ground truth in gt/ocr, the body column runs 1774-1797 px wide, median ~1780, across all three parts. So a fixed-width column is a real constraint rather than an approximation imposed on the page.
_provenance.anchor: Where that column SITS is not stable, and this is the finding that shaped the design. Measured over the rasters, the left edge of the text drifts 399-760 px within part 1, 342-462 within part 2 and 310-546 within part 3 — up to 236 px inside a single part, and up to 170 px between pages of the same scan-index parity. That is scan registration, not typography: the width barely moves while the position wanders. A per-part constant column was therefore wrong by ~100 px on most pages (it put 1-048's column at 618..2410 where the page actually sets 722..2498), and verso/recto could not rescue it because parity explains only part of the drift. The column is now anchored PER PAGE off the raster's own ink profile.
_provenance.calibration: ink_pad_left / ink_pad_right convert the measured ink edge into the text-column edge, and are calibrated against the 20 gt/ocr pages: the ink profile lands a mean +17 px inside the true left edge and -11 px inside the true right, because a line box carries a little air beyond its ink. Applying those two offsets reproduces the true column on all 20 within 7 px.
_provenance.runs: The edge comes from runs of inked columns, not from the outermost inked column, and that distinction is the whole robustness of the thing. Density cannot discriminate: 1-033 carries a long mark in its left margin whose densest column holds 774 inked rows — more than any column of type on the same page — and it dragged the anchor 52 px left. Width can: the smudge is a 10 px run, the text block a 1746 px one. So runs narrower than `min_run_px` are dropped as specks, and the column is the SPAN from the first surviving run to the last. The span rather than a single run, because a sparse page — a chapter opening, a short closing page — fragments: 1-022 yields nine runs of which the widest is 863 px against a 1778 px measure, and demanding one run the width of the measure sent it to the fallback with the column 245 px out. `min_run_share` is what the span must reach to be believed. Calibrated against both witnesses: 7 px worst-case against the 20 line-precise gt/ocr pages, 11 px against the 45 pages keyed by hand.
_provenance.overrides: Pages the anchor cannot serve — two-column settings above all, and near-blank plates where there is not enough ink to measure. 1-330 is the worked example of the second kind: its widest ink run is 80 px, so detection is refused and the fallback applies.

view._about: The editor's default framing. `column_margin` is the share of the text-column width left as breathing room either side when the page is first sized — the column is what is being judged, so it gets the viewport, not the leaf. The view is also cropped vertically to the page's own inked band plus `content_pad_px`, which is what takes an ordinary leaf from three screens to two: the top and bottom of a scan are blank paper and scrolling through them is time spent on nothing. That pad is not only cosmetic — it is the strip a pointer overshoots into, and overshooting the top or bottom of the view is how a zone is run to the first or last line of the page without pixel-hunting the boundary, so it has to be wide enough to aim at. `content_ink_fraction` is the share of the page width a row must be dark to count as printed, taken from the width rather than from the densest row so that one black photograph cannot raise the bar above the type beside it. Hovering within `edge_band_px` of the top or bottom of the view jumps a whole screen, instantly, keeping `edge_overlap_px` of what was already showing. It fires once per entry into the band — the cursor has to leave and come back — so a jump can never run away.

columns._about: The measure is configured; the position is measured off each page. See _provenance.anchor for why that split exists. The measures survived the move into master space untouched, because a width does not change under a translation — only the positional fallback_x0 shifted, by each part's dx: part 1 500->479, part 3 380->415, part 2 unmoved.

overrides._about: Per-ref column windows for pages the anchor cannot serve — two-column settings, and plates with too little ink to measure. A ref listed here replaces the measured column for that page entirely; the UI's column cycle walks whatever list it finds. Keyed PP-NNN, same as everything else.

paragraph_split._about: Splitting one body band back into its paragraphs, off the raster. The segmenter cannot do this and never will: two adjacent MainZone-P zones abut, so they rasterize into one continuous training target and the boundary is destroyed before the network ever sees it. 42% of all consecutive zone pairs in gt/zones/ are same-label (596 of 1405, 561 abutting, 568 paragraph-to-paragraph), so this is not an edge case — it is nearly half the boundaries in the corpus. The ink still knows: a paragraph's first line is indented. Calibrated over 60 pages, 177 true starts against 1280 mid-paragraph lines: at 40 px it finds 96.6% of starts with 0.4% false, and the false rate is flat from 30 to 80 px, so the remainder is a separate population rather than a threshold artifact. The ragged right margin was measured too and rejected: paragraphs that happen to end flush make its p10 (24 px) overlap the mid-line p90 (21 px). min_line_w_px exists because five of the first twenty false hits were 4-21 px specks in the right margin — dirt, not type.
paragraph_split._margin_pct_about: An indent is measured against the margin the page's body sets, and that margin used to be the MINIMUM left edge over the column strip — which hands the whole page's typography to whichever line carries the leftmost speck of dirt. 1-160 is the worked example: prose set beside a figure with a dozen flecks scattered down the gutter between them, 4-10 px each. min_line_w_px cannot reach one, since the run it shares rows with is a whole line wide, so the leftmost became the margin, every clean line then read 40-47 px against the 40 px floor, and tei generate cut 20 paragraphs into a page keyed as 3. Corpus-wide that failure was 96 of the 118 false positives, on five pages (1-160, 1-188, 1-194, 2-068, 2-088), each with the same signature: a tight band of near-identical indents just over threshold, which is a mis-set margin and not a page of one-line paragraphs. The margin is now the margin_pct-th percentile of the strip's left edges, which spends that share of the strip on dirt and asks the rest to agree. Calibrated over the whole store against the same audit the recall figure comes from — false positives run 118/46/33/28/25 at 0/10/15/20/25 and flatten there (25, 24, 22 at 33/40/50), while false negatives run 53/55/55/55/55 then 56/58/62. 25 is the knee: the false positives have bottomed out and the false negatives are still on their plateau. Two refinements were measured and REJECTED, and are recorded because both sound right: a rolling window tracking the margin down the page bought nothing at 21 lines and lost recall at 11 (this book drifts between pages, not within one), and restricting the statistic to lines justified to the measure lost 18 boundaries at the median (a paragraph's last line is short and flush left, so it is one of the best witnesses to a LEFT margin there is — where a line ends bears on nothing here).
paragraph_split._consolidate_about: A cut lands at the top of the opening line, so whatever sat above it — the whitespace between paragraphs, or a speck the line detector mistook for a line — is left as its own sliver. Those are invisible in the editor and are not zones: `min_zone_h_px` already says a band that short cannot be one. So a fragment under that height is folded into a neighbour, **and only into one carrying the same label**. `down` gives it to the paragraph below, which is right when the sliver is leading whitespace; `up` gives it to the one above; where only one side matches, that side wins regardless. Where neither matches the sliver stays and `validate_page` reports it as min-height, which is a finding about the decode rather than something to paper over.

train_merges._about: Classes the *segmenter* is not asked to tell apart, applied by `harness zones --assemble` when it builds the training copies and nowhere else. The editor still offers every type, `gt/zones/` still stores what was keyed, and every check still reads the keyed label — a distinction a human drew is evidence and is not destroyed to suit a model. Read the measurement before adding one, and record it here: this file is where a fold has to be arguable.

MainZone-Quote.why: Block quote and 'other' are set at the same size with the same measure, and the model cannot separate them: of 31 MainZone-Quote regions it drew over the held-out pages, 6 were right and 23 were really MainZone-Other, while 15 of MainZone-Other's misses were really Quote — 38 zones swapped, the largest single error in the matrix. Folding them for training raises held-out precision 61.3% -> 78.2% and recall 93.9% -> 94.9%. Quote was also the class this design was already unsure of: zero instances at 75 pages, 25 at 181, joint-smallest either way.
